title: RoundGuard: Exact Attainable Discrepancies in Monetary Rounding Policies
affiliation: Economics and Management School, Wuhan University
abstract: Exact decimal arithmetic does not determine when a monetary calculation should be rounded. A line-item rule and its aggregate counterpart can produce different payable amounts even when both use exact rational intermediates. Universal rounding bounds do not tell a developer whether their endpoints are attainable on the permitted amount grids. We present RoundGuard, an exact analyzer for explicitly declared monetary rounding policies. For rational affine expressions with translation-compatible quantizers, it computes structural shifts and compares policies on feasible residue representatives. For independent affine line items, a cyclic residue dynamic program (DP) computes attainable signed discrepancy extrema and reconstructs inputs achieving them, without enumerating the Cartesian input grid. Its operation count is pseudo-polynomial in a common denominator; sign-sensitive modes require a proved nonnegative-line condition or an unreduced satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) fallback. A JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) rule interface supports six rounding modes, finite placement families, and bounded piecewise expressions. Independent exhaustive decimal evaluation checks the analyzer on synthetic, canonical, and public-rule-derived fragments. Scaling experiments compare the dynamic program with full-grid SMT and a residue-reduced SMT ablation. The contribution is a specialized analysis of feasible monetary discrepancies built on established shift-periodic arithmetic and min/max-plus dynamic programming, rather than a new general theory of rounding.
comments: 13 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Code and reproducible artifact: https://github.com/beibeihk/roundguard
